This is a detailed, function-by-function review of the three complete modules (and a note on the truncated fourth). I will organize by file, then by function/class, calling out concrete bugs, edge cases, and refactoring opportunities.

## File: `serve/__init__.py`

This file is essentially a one-line docstring. There is nothing to review beyond the trivial: the package exposes no public API from `__init__.py`, which is fine if everything is imported by full path. One minor note: if a downstream consumer ever does `from serve import *`, they will get nothing useful. That is intentional, but a `__all__` or at least a comment clarifying "this is a namespace-only package" would help readers avoid confusion during refactoring.

---

## File: `serve/frontend.py`

### Class: `TemplateRequestError`

```python
class TemplateRequestError(jinja2.exceptions.TemplateError, ValueError):
```

**Edge case / potential bug:** Multiple inheritance from `jinja2.exceptions.TemplateError` and `ValueError` relies on both being exceptions and on the MRO not conflicting. In practice this works because `TemplateError` inherits from `Exception` and `ValueError` inherits from `Exception`, so the MRO resolves to `(TemplateRequestError, TemplateError, ValueError, Exception, ...)`. This is fine, but it is fragile if Jinja2 ever changes `TemplateError` to no longer be a direct child of `Exception` (it is today, via `BaseException`). A `try/except (TemplateError, ValueError)` catch at the call site would also need to be checked; if the caller only catches `ValueError`, the `TemplateError` half is still caught because of the MRO. This is correct but subtle — a short comment in the docstring explaining the multi-inheritance rationale would help.
